cards.text: ELEANOR — EUROPEAN TRAVEL STORYBOARD

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: One Cognac Eleanor, three European travel looks. The approved AI UGC script moves from Paris ease to Milan polish and London personality, then returns to looking put together between cities. Persistent Eurofall presenter over distinct fashion images; aspiration leads and function supports. Actual selected first-frame images are attached. All timings are provisional.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: If you're going to Europe this fall, here's how I'd style one beautiful travel bag for Paris, Milan and London. Three different looks, without buying a whole new wardrobe for every stop.
Opening: three distinct European outfit scenes; same Eleanor, three looks. Presenter stays lower-left.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Desire / hook. The immediately readable outfits make the European wardrobe promise concrete. Three new locations preview the city chapters; walking starts on frame one. This is fashion aspiration rather than distress.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. First-frame asset for Google Omni motion; action at normal pace. Main image demonstrates finished overlay placement; clean hook plate is in the support lane.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This is the Eleanor Weekender from Velantra. I'd go for Cognac.
Cognac Eleanor rests on limestone console; complete front, flap and handles.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Product introduction. A quiet whole-bag view establishes the item the narrator names and a stable visual identity before the city looks. Cut on “This is the Eleanor Weekender”.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. Held photo; no automatic zoom or transition preset.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: That warm leather against the light canvas gives you such a beautiful starting point for your travel outfits.
Close detail: cognac leather, light canvas, stitching and horizontal gold fitting.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. Held photo; no automatic zoom or transition preset.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Starting with Paris, I'd keep everything relaxed. Straight-leg jeans, a cream knit, a trench and loafers. Then carry the Eleanor by the top handles. The bag gives those simple pieces a more finished look, even when you're just arriving at your hotel.
Paris: brunette model steps through hotel entrance in trench, cream knit, jeans and loafers.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Attainable aspiration. Familiar jeans, knit and loafers make Paris styling easy to imagine. The hotel-arrival action connects the full outfit to travel; hold long enough to read shoes and bag together.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. First-frame asset for Google Omni motion; action at normal pace.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: For Milan, I'd dress it up. Tailored trousers, a fitted knit, a long coat,
Milan: same model in camel coat, espresso knit and charcoal tailoring in a marble lobby.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Polish / styling demonstration. Sharper trousers and coat change the same bag’s mood. A new lobby and full-body composition clearly separate Milan from the Paris doorway.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. First-frame asset for Google Omni motion; action at normal pace.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: and a little gold jewelry to pick up the hardware. The same bag suddenly feels much more polished because of what you've put around it.
Milan detail: bracelet, knit cuff and hand carrying the rolled handles beside gold fitting.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Detail demonstration. The bracelet and bag fitting share a warm metal tone, explaining the specific styling suggestion visually. Cut on “and a little gold jewelry”; keep both elements readable through the rest of the sentence and its payoff.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. Held photo; no automatic zoom or transition preset.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And for London, I'd have a little more fun. A checked jacket, relaxed trousers, comfortable sneakers. Let the textures do the work. The canvas and leather sit so nicely alongside those autumn layers.
London: checked jacket, relaxed trousers and sneakers; hand closes around handles to begin lifting Eleanor from bench.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Personality / practical support. Checks, sneakers and a new pickup action show relaxed travel styling. Enter on London, preserve the whole look and let the pickup complete before leaving the scene.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. First-frame asset for Google Omni motion; action at normal pace.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: That's what I like about building your travel wardrobe around a bag like this. You can change the whole mood with your clothes, and your weekender still feels like part of the outfit.
Wardrobe: Eleanor in foreground, three coordinated clothing groups behind it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Understanding / recap. The clothes rail collects the three styling approaches around one bag after the examples establish them. A fresh still helps the viewer understand the wardrobe principle without replaying prior footage.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. Held photo; no automatic zoom or transition preset.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Because the outfit you wear between cities deserves just as much thought as the one you wear when you get there.
Travel payoff: model adjusts coat at train doorway, Eleanor in her other hand.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Desired journey. Adjusting the coat while arriving by train makes between-city dressing feel intentional. This travel action pays off the script’s central idea after the wardrobe recap.

Direct background cuts; continuous presenter and narration. Timing provisional until final voice alignment. First-frame asset for Google Omni motion; action at normal pace.

cards.text: So, Paris, Milan or London—which look would you wear? Shop the Eleanor Weekender at Velantra.

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: APPROVED WORDS
cards.text: The approved 246-word script is preserved exactly across the yellow cards. Estimated runtime is about 84 seconds including the end hold; re-align after voice selection.

cards.title: PRESENTER THROUGHOUT
cards.text: Use P01, the selected Eurofall presenter identity, as the continuous lower-left guide. L01 shows the hook layout. Background cards retain clean images for motion and editing. Keep face, bag, hands and footwear clear.

cards.title: VOICE & CAPTIONS
cards.text: Warm conversational styling advice, natural emphasis on the city names. Continuous speech, white outlined phrase captions matched to the approved words. City labels mark the chapters. No testimonial or nationality claim.

cards.title: SOUND & CLOSE
cards.text: Optional quiet instrumental bed beneath clear dialogue; no decorative whooshes. Fade music over the last two seconds. O01 supplies the closing graphic. Confirm exact voice alignment before locking cuts.

cards.title: ELEANOR IDENTITY
cards.text: Cognac: ivory woven canvas, cognac leather, horizontal center oval, open flap-wing slots and continuous short closure straps. Current corrected creative reference and physical-detail evidence used. Physical scale is not certified by generated images.

cards.title: PRODUCTION HANDOFF
cards.text: 13 new GPT Image 2 images supplied: ten scene plates, presenter, hook layout and closing overlay. Scene plates are first frames where motion is planned. Google Omni for video; DaVinci Resolve for assembly. No finished video or voiceover is included.

cards.title: REFERENCE LIMIT
cards.text: Source: Sara Ouardi’s linked Instagram reel. 43 chronological samples and 33 adjacent-frame picture changes reviewed during script development. This is an adaptation of city styling logic, not a claim of an exhaustive frame/audio match.
